solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Memorial to encapsulate drinking venue in Ireland, say

indicators.note: to encapsulate means the first piece wraps around the second like a capsule

parts.note: a relic is a memorial or keepsake of something past
a pub is a place for drinking

explanation.surface: Plans for a monument that will enclose a bar somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is one example of a state governed without a monarch, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Repeat aloud name supporting engineers

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to cite is to name or quote as an example

explanation.surface: Someone repeats the name of the person backing the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say something out loud from memory.

clue.text: Irishman and Arab entertained by wealthy venerable figure

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name in crosswords

indicators.note: entertained by means the piece is taken inside the next word

parts.note: rich means wealthy
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Irishman and an Arab are hosted by a rich elder statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is a respected elderly man heading a family or church.

clue.text: Banker abroad taking in cold hillside feature?

indicators.note: taking in means the rearranged letters enclose another
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A banker overseas catches a chill out on the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: BANKER rearranged gives BRAKEN, with C inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is the fern that typically covers British hillsides, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stupid piece of abject penitence brought up

indicators.note: brought up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clumsy act of grovelling repentance gets mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is the signal that the letters sit within the phrase; in a down clue 'brought up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means foolishly clumsy, and 'stupid piece' is the definition read as a clumsy item.

clue.text: Message given after departure cancelled? A swindle

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the message on a gravestone after someone departs this life
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: Someone finds the trip they paid for has been called off and suspects they were conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departure' here means death, not leaving on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is an informal noun for a fraud or overcharging scam.

clue.text: Grab young offender on ship

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
re means on or concerning
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster on board is seized.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress once meant to seize men forcibly for naval service, so it can mean grab.

clue.text: Aquatic creature is more animated? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: hotter can mean more heated or excited

explanation.surface: Is a river animal livelier? Not to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a mammal that lives in rivers and swims well.

clue.text: Asian type of pastry I secure inside

indicators.note: inside means the following pieces go within the pastry word

parts.note: filo is a thin flaky pastry
to pin is to fasten or secure

explanation.surface: A recipe step: fasten the filling inside a pastry case.
explanation.definitionFit: A Filipino is a person from the Philippines, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Solid Tory found on island

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician discovered on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits above the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means solid, real and tangible rather than abstract.

clue.text: Unconventional place to go at this medical institution

indicators.note: unconventional means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: the fodder, fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd place to visit, this clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to go' tempts a toilet reading; all four words plus 'this' are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural hospital in Britain, often staffed by local GPs, is known by this name.

clue.text: Tinker adjusted front of tatty small ornament

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of the word before it are rearranged
front of picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tinker fiddles with a cheap, shabby knick-knack.
explanation.walkthrough: The tinker looks like the person in the scene, but the word is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a cheap little decorative item or bauble.

clue.text: Comfort achieved in Switzerland with soup on reflection

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: on reflection says the word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: a purée is a thick blended soup

explanation.surface: Someone finds solace in a Swiss bowl of soup after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieved in' and 'with' are link words; CH is the Swiss country code from the Latin Confoederatio Helvetica.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to console them and lift their spirits.

clue.text: French city largely developed by titled figure

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: grew means developed or got bigger
a noble is someone holding an aristocratic title

explanation.surface: A French town expanded thanks to a local aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps.

clue.text: Car's back by river overlooking quiet military establishment

parts.note: the boot is the storage space at the rear of a British car
the Cam is the river through Cambridge
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A car's rear parked by a river above a calm training base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'overlooking' place the pieces in order down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is a training base for new military recruits.

clue.text: In which one might see hairdressers alone? On the contrary

definitions.text: In which one might see hairdressers

indicators.note: on the contrary flips the opening: rather than the hairdressers being in the place, the place is in the words hairdressers alone

parts.note: the run spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Wondering where one finds hairdressers working on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads as a definition; 'On the contrary' then says the place sits within 'hairdressers alone' instead of the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's shop is commonly called a hair salon.

clue.text: Hateful motel has collapsed with nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the zero is placed within the rearranged letters
collapsed means the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dreadful motel has fallen down and nothing is left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means detestable, causing hatred or disgust.

clue.text: Woman shaking hand in roofed terrace

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

indicators.note: shaking means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman shakes hands out on a covered patio.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed platform along the outside of a house.

clue.text: English people objectively missing at end distinctive character

indicators.note: missing at end means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: 'those' can stand for people as the object of a sentence, as in 'those who wait'

explanation.surface: Englishmen viewed dispassionately are said to lack a certain closing flourish in their character.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a group or era.

clue.text: Release second film without a charge

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A second movie shown at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release from captivity.

clue.text: Writer in work left a note describing modern offices?

indicators.note: in means the writer is placed inside the word for work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a pen is a writing instrument
N is short for note, as in an abbreviation

explanation.surface: An author at work jots down a description of contemporary office design.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern offices are often laid out with no partition walls, one large shared space.

clue.text: Study country with society above a lake

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

explanation.surface: Looking into a nation whose social life sits above a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination.

clue.text: Patron having small change (about pound I detected)

indicators.note: about means the coin word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A customer is caught with loose change and a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a customer, someone who patronises a business.

clue.text: Severe figure when with football team league's dropped

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is removed from the team name

parts.note: Celtic is a Glasgow football club
L is the abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: A stern character appears after a football team is relegated from its league.
explanation.walkthrough: CELTIC, a Scottish football club, loses its L to give CETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone practising severe self-denial, an austere person.

clue.text: Prank produced by person in temporary site miles away

indicators.note: away means the named letter goes from the word

parts.note: a camper stays in a tent or camp, a temporary site

explanation.surface: Someone at a campsite pulls a stunt far from anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful escapade or prank.

clue.text: Legal officer concerned with the military we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: martial means relating to war or armed forces

explanation.surface: An officer of the court who deals with the army, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a marshal is a federal law-enforcement officer attached to the courts.

clue.text: Cut rodents besetting bottom of garden

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the rodents enclose the letter

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: bottom of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Chop the mice infesting the end of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to cut food into very small pieces.

clue.text: Tradesmen potter about in large retail site

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Workmen wander aimlessly around a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' looks like a craftsman but is only letters; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store is a big shop divided into sections selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Watford player, one with a buzz?

definitions.meaning: Watford FC, an English football club
a large wasp makes a buzzing sound

explanation.surface: A footballer from Watford with a lot of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Watford's players are called after this stinging insect, which buzzes as it flies.

clue.text: Miserable place around North Elizabeth's found showing huge determination

parts.note: hell is the most miserable place imaginable

indicators.note: around means the short name wraps the abbreviation for north

parts.note: Bet is a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth, discovered in a grim northern spot, is fiercely resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly set on doing something, utterly determined.
